summary: The appeal challenged the Allahabad High Court's acquittal of accused persons in a case involving murder under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC. The prosecution relied on two dying declarations—one recorded by police under Cr.PC Section 161 and another by a Magistrate/SDM. The Trial Court had convicted the accused, relying on the Magistrate-recorded dying declaration, but the High Court acquitted, distrusting both declarations due to inconsistency and lack of corroboration. The Supreme Court considered whether multiple dying declarations render the evidence unreliable per se, and whether the Magistrate’s version could sustain conviction. It emphasized that a dying declaration before a Magistrate carries greater weight, especially when no malice is shown, and that multiple declarations do not automatically invalidate each other. The Court found the High Court erred in rejecting the Magistrate-recorded declaration without valid reason.

final_judgment: The appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment of the High Court acquitting the accused is set aside. The conviction and sentence imposed by the Trial Court under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC are restored. The accused shall surrender forthwith to serve the remaining sentence.
